explanation: Johnson never cites McEwen; it cites Smith v. State, 302 Ark. 459 (sharing a S.W.2d page cite) for the directed-verdict standard. Sutton overruled McEwen only on felon/firearm joinder prejudice, a different point.
Welch cites Kavanaugh v. Baird only on res judicata/lack of identity of parties. Hilt overruled it on Great Lakes title between meander line and water, a different proposition; negation not on point.

Yurina cites Anderson for no double jeopardy in using priors both as aggravator and habitual enhancement. Rhyne overruled Anderson only on imposing a separate habitual sentence rather than enhancing a felony sentence; different point.

Joy relies on Green only for conviction on uncorroborated accomplice testimony, which Turner reaffirmed. Turner disapproved only the cautionary-scrutiny statement, which Joy recites as defendant's argument and declines to apply.

South Carolina court twice cites the Arizona Court of Appeals Camargo opinion as authority that independent verification/controlled buy shows informant reliability, though the Arizona Supreme Court vacated that opinion outright in 1975; no history noted; unrelated litigation.

Slider cites Klasing (see also, p. 732) for employee procuring own medical treatment when employer neglects to furnish it. Mills overruled Klasing on construing the $3,600 average-annual-earnings exclusion; different point.

Sims quotes The Harrisburg, via Western Loan, for a statutory time limit conditioning the right itself. Moragne overruled only the holding that general maritime law gives no wrongful-death action; that limitation principle was untouched.
